title: TrustContext
description: Trust level attached to every piece of content entering a turn. This is the mechanism that makes prompt injection structurally unable to escalate privilege, rather than filtered and hoped about (ADR-0012).

compatibility.notes: Adding a trust level is a MAJOR change. Levels are totally ordered and the ordering is load-bearing: policy compares them numerically. Inserting a level renumbers the ordinals and silently changes every policy decision. If a level must be added, it goes at an end and the ordinals are re-derived in a new major version.

level.description: The EFFECTIVE trust of the turn. Equals the MINIMUM level across all entries in `sources`. Never computed any other way.

sources.description: Every distinct origin of content that has entered this turn's context. Append-only within a turn.

degraded_at.description: When the effective level last decreased. Null if the turn has never degraded.

degraded_by.description: source_id of the entry that caused the most recent degradation. Populated for audit and for explaining a refusal to the user.

TrustLevel.description:
Totally ordered, most trusted first. ordinal: operator=3, user_originated=2, tool_result=1, external_content=0.

- operator        Efe acting deliberately outside a conversation (config, an approved commit).
- user_originated Content spoken or typed by Efe in this turn.
- tool_result     Output of a tool L.I.O.N.E.L invoked. Trusted less than speech because a tool can return attacker-controlled bytes.
- external_content A file, web page, email, or document. ASSUME HOSTILE.

origin.description: memory_recall inherits the level stored on the MemoryRecord. A memory ingested from external_content stays external_content forever — laundering content through memory must not upgrade it.

detail.description: Human-readable provenance for the audit log. Path, URL, or tool name.
